correctness.rationale: For all 0<alpha<beta<=4 and every finite equality-invariant S, injectivity of one logistic restriction implies both maps permute S, contradicting unequal positive scaling unless S={0}; hence distinct complementary points occur. Nontrivial equality invariance supplies an interior point, separately preperiodic under both maps, so it solves two explicit polynomial equations. Endpoint-factor removal is valid, their resultants are nonzero by specialization alpha=2 and nonvanishing partner polynomials, and their zero sets are proper algebraic sets. Degree counting bounds partner parameters by B_N^2, proving measure-zero, meagre, and countable-section conclusions. Exact checker tests small-order quotient/resultant identities and edge examples; an all-order analytic argument establishes the theorem.

value.rationale: Recent logistic-IFS literature classifies small finite switching structures along exceptional curves but does not provide a universal criterion across all support sizes. The forced fold-collision lemma and constructive proper algebraic locus P_N give a size-independent structural obstruction. The finite bound on partner parameters allows algebraic filtering of all bounded-size candidates and the null/meagre theorem shows that exceptional finite structures never fill a positive-area parameter region. This is a directly motivated all-cardinality conclusion, not a recomputation of one small invariant set. Necessary conditions may overcount; no attraction or complete enumeration is claimed.
